details:
Sinavigator is an interactive lunar exploration platform developed to support the analysis and visualization of potential lunar landing locations. It combines 3D visualization, lunar terrain data, and astronomical calculations to examine how the positions of the Sun and Earth affect visibility from selected locations on the lunar surface.

Users can explore the Moon through an interactive Lunar Atlas, inspect terrain, analyze local horizons, and compare visibility conditions across different time periods using a timeline-based scenario system. The platform also includes educational features that make lunar navigation concepts easier to understand.

Built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Three.js, Python, and FastAPI, Sinavigator integrates scientific data processing with an accessible web interface. We used resources from NASA and JPL to support the terrain and astronomical analysis.

Our goal is to make complex lunar environment data easier to explore and interpret, while demonstrating how interactive software can support future lunar mission research and education. We considered terrain characteristics, solar visibility, Earth visibility, temporal changes, data availability, and the limitations of geometric modeling throughout development.
